title: Risks of the built-in executors
context: Why is using the built-in Executors factory methods discouraged?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `Executors.newFixedThreadPool` and `newSingleThreadExecutor` use an unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue, so queued tasks can grow until memory runs out. `newCachedThreadPool` and `newScheduledThreadPool` can create threads without a limit (cached) or grow the queue (scheduled). Build a ThreadPoolExecutor directly, with a bounded queue, a max pool size, a named ThreadFactory and a rejection policy. Then the limits are visible in the code.

points.title: Unbounded queue
points.why: A default fixed pool queues without limit, and memory grows until OutOfMemoryError.

points.title: Unbounded threads
points.why: Cached pools create a thread per task when none is idle.
